sentence_stem: Not only did the new policy reduce costs,
correct_completion: but it also improved customer satisfaction.
full_sentence: Not only did the new policy reduce costs, but it also improved customer satisfaction.
acceptable_variants: but it also raised the quality of service.
but it also made the company more competitive.

options.text: so the company decided to close two branches.
options.why_wrong: This gives a consequence, but 'not only ... but also' requires an additional positive result of the same kind.

options.text: but it also improved customer satisfaction.
although customers still complained about delays.
options.why_wrong: 'Although' introduces a contrast that breaks the additive structure 'not only ... but also'.

options.text: because the costs had been rising for years.
options.why_wrong: This explains a cause, but the stem's correlative structure needs a second benefit, not a reason.

grammar_focus: Correlative conjunction 'not only ... but also' for additive cohesion
explanation: The stem opens a correlative pair, so the completion must add a second benefit that matches the first in form and meaning. Learners often choose a clause that introduces a cause or a contrast, which breaks the additive relationship. Check that the second half adds a parallel idea rather than explaining or opposing the first.
